newsitem.title: UK: British Jews urge Arafat to act on bombings.
newsitem.headline: British Jews urge Arafat to act on bombings.

text.p: Jewish leaders in Britain on Monday urged Palestinian President Yasser Arafat to track down those behind last week's twin suicide bombings in a Jerusalem market.

The Board of Deputies of British Jews, which speaks for the Jewish community, said its president, Eldred Tabachnik, had sent a personal message to Arafat in reponse to last Wednesday's bombings that killed 13 people and wounded 170.
Tabachnik condemned the bombings as "a brutal attack which showed no mercy and was calculated to cause the maximum number of fatalities".
He hoped that Arafat would "make every effort to track down those responsible for this appalling deed and ensure that they are tried and convicted.
"This is a time when all partners to the peace process must show that they are determined to secure justice for yesterday's victims, who were so callously denied any semblance of justice."
Eldred called for the peace process to be resumed in an attempt to reach a just and peaceful solution.
